findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key appended as query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: The server rejects api_key query parameter with HTTP 401 ('send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'). API key must be sent in the X-API-Key HTTP header.
findings.how_found: Sent a GET request to /v1/listings with api_key query parameter and inspected the 401 error response body.
findings.impact: Requests with query param fail authentication; all client requests must set X-API-Key header.

findings.documented: Tokens are valid for 24 hours (expires_in: 86400), so a single login is enough for one session. There is no refresh flow. User object returns name and email.
findings.actual: Login response returns 'access_token' with expires_in: 900 (15 minutes), includes 'refresh_token' and 'refresh_url': '/auth/refresh', and user object only contains 'email' (no 'name'). Token refresh is supported at POST /auth/refresh.
findings.how_found: Invoked POST /auth/login and inspected returned JSON keys, expiry timestamp, and tested POST /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: Sessions expire after 15 minutes instead of 24 hours; clients must implement refresh token rotation to maintain persistent user sessions.

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: POST /auth/logout returns { ok: true, note: 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side' } without performing server-side revocation.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout and verified that existing JWT tokens remain cryptographically valid until expiration.
findings.impact: Client-side session clearing in localStorage is required upon logout.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page (1-indexed) and limit (default 20, max 200). Shape: {total, page, page_size, results}.
findings.actual: Pagination ignores 'page' parameter and requires 'offset' and 'limit'. Maximum limit is capped at 50 records (requesting limit=100 or 200 returns count=50). Response shape is {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results}.
findings.how_found: Tested GET /v1/listings with page=2 vs offset=50 and limit=100. Inspected JSON metadata keys and record offsets.
findings.impact: Requesting page=2 returns offset=0 (page 1 again); applications must use limit/offset to page across the full catalog.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing object.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns HTTP 404 Not Found. The working endpoint is plural: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Executed GET requests against both /v1/listing/{id} (404) and /v1/listings/{id} (200).
findings.impact: Calls to documented singular endpoint fail; frontend routes must call /v1/listings/{id}.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.how_found: Invoked GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar for multiple valid listing IDs.
findings.impact: Recommendation strip cannot rely on backend endpoint; client-side similarity heuristic required.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} manage user saved listings.
findings.actual: Endpoints return HTTP 404 Not Found across all HTTP methods.
findings.how_found: Tested GET, POST, and DELETE on /v1/favourites and /v1/favorites.
findings.impact: User saved listings must be persisted locally in browser localStorage scoped per user email.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for the city.
findings.impact: Dashboard analytics must be computed dynamically in the application layer from ingested datasets.

findings.documented: Supports server-side filtering via min_price, max_price, furnishing, bedroom, and project_id.
findings.actual: Parameters min_price, max_price, furnishing, bedroom, and project_id are quietly ignored by the server (total matches remain 4084). Only locality, bhk, and property_type are filtered server-side.
findings.how_found: Sent requests with min_price=10000000, furnishing=semi-furnished, bedroom=2 and verified total count and results remained unconstrained.
findings.impact: Frontend must apply client-side filtering fallbacks to ensure user filter selections take effect.

findings.documented: sort_by=price&order=asc sorts listings by ascending sale price.
findings.actual: Server executes direct database order without filtering out corrupt negative price records, placing records with negative prices at the top of results.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings?sort_by=price&order=asc and observed negative price listings returned as first items.
findings.impact: Clients must filter corrupt negative values before presenting sorted listings to users.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Project price_min and price_max are floating-point numbers in mixed Indian denominations: values < 10 represent Crores (10^7 INR) and values >= 10 represent Lakhs (10^5 INR).
findings.how_found: Analyzed price_min and price_max across all 450 projects and cross-referenced with linked listing prices.
findings.impact: Raw project prices displayed without conversion are off by a factor of 100,000 to 10,000,000.

findings.documented: Area is in Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: A subset of listings have carpet_area values recorded in square meters (e.g., 70-150 sqm for 2-3 BHK units) rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Analyzed carpet_area distributions across bedroom counts and identified clusters corresponding to square meters.
findings.impact: Unconverted area values distort price-per-sqft calculations and filter accuracy.

findings.documented: Timestamps are in ISO 8601, UTC, with 'Z' suffix everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Listing posted_at timestamps omit the 'Z' suffix and timezone offset (e.g., '2026-08-29T20:53:00'), and several records carry future timestamps in 2027.
findings.how_found: Inspected posted_at string format across all listing records and compared with /health server clock.
findings.impact: Naive UTC parsers miscalculate listing ages by 5.5 hours without explicit IST offset handling.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns 855 inactive records where is_live=false alongside active records.
findings.how_found: Filtered retrievable listings by is_live boolean property.
findings.impact: Frontend must filter on is_live == true to avoid displaying expired or withdrawn inventory.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Multiple listing records across different portals describe the exact same physical property (matching apartment name, locality, floor, total floors, BHK, bathroom, carpet area, and facing direction).
findings.how_found: Constructed multidimensional composite property keys to cluster identical property specifications across portal feeds.
findings.impact: Aggregations that assume 1 listing = 1 unique property overestimate distinct available inventory.

findings.documented: Listing records accurately describe genuine property specifications.
findings.actual: Dataset contains corrupt records describing impossible properties (floor > total_floors, carpet_area > super_built_up_area, negative prices).
findings.how_found: Ran constraint validation rules checking floor <= total_floors, carpet <= super_built_up, and non-negative numeric fields.
findings.impact: Corrupt records produce invalid property cards and corrupt statistical metrics if not sanitized.

findings.documented: All listings are verified properties for sale.
findings.actual: Dataset contains fake listings created to harvest user enquiries, demanding advance booking fees before site visits or advertising urgent below-market bait.
findings.how_found: Audited description texts with regex patterns for token fees and urgency bait phrases, plus sub-50k sale prices.
findings.impact: Scam listings present user trust and safety risks; flagged and filtered in production views.

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: For 346 of 450 projects, total_listings does not match the actual number of listings linked to project_id in /v1/listings.
findings.how_found: Grouped /v1/listings by project_id and compared actual counts against project total_listings field.
findings.impact: Project cards display inaccurate inventory counts unless recomputed from the live listings collection.
